title: Visualizing the CDF of the Maximum of Two Random Variables
full_prompt: Write a Manim script (compatible with ManimGL/InteractiveScene) that visualizes the probability distribution of the maximum of two independent uniform random variables. First, set up a 2D coordinate system (Axes) ranging from 0 to 1 on both axes. Create a custom helper function to generate a random variable label group containing a ValueTracker, an ArrowTip pointing at the axis, and a Tex label (e.g., 'x_1' in blue for the x-axis, 'x_2' in yellow for the y-axis). Implement two custom Animation classes: 1) 'TrackingDots' which leaves a trail of glowing dots (GlowDot) at the tracked coordinate, and 2) 'Randomize' which rapidly updates a ValueTracker with random values to simulate sampling. Animate the introduction of the x_1 tracker, run the randomization animation with tracking dots along the x-axis, and then highlight a specific interval (a < x_1 < b) using a colored SurroundingRectangle and display the corresponding probability equation 'P(a < x_1 < b) = b - a'.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Using Manim Community Scene instead of InteractiveScene when utilizing specific ManimGL features
common_failure_modes.note: The reference code relies on InteractiveScene and specific updater syntax like 'always.next_to' which is unique to ManimGL.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Missing custom GlowDot or TrackingDots implementation
common_failure_modes.note: The visual trail effect relies on the custom TrackingDots animation class. Substituting with standard static dots loses the dynamic sampling feel.
